# Challenge set, model arm: what the verifier catches that rules cannot

<!-- Generated by scripts/run_challenge_model_arm.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

The rules-only arm (`reports/challenge_rules.md`) catches every citation corruption and **none** of the semantic ones, which is structural: a reversed edge keeps the same two variables, the same passage and the same verbatim span, so no deterministic rule can see it. This arm measures the verifier on exactly those items.

| Corruption family | Items | Scored | Flagged | Rate | Rules could see it? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| inflated_strength | 15 | 15 | 8 | 0.533 | no, by construction |
| reversed_relation | 23 | 23 | 9 | 0.391 | no, by construction |
| unsupported_intermediate | 23 | 23 | 23 | 1.000 | yes, rejected before the model |
| wrong_date | 23 | 23 | 23 | 1.000 | yes, rejected before the model |
| wrong_target | 23 | 23 | 23 | 1.000 | yes, rejected before the model |

**False-alarm rate on the 23 clean controls: 0.087.** Unscored controls: 0. Strength disagreements on controls, reported separately and not counted as false alarms: 8.

## The number this arm exists for

**17 of 38 semantic corruptions caught** (0.447), against **0 of 38** for the rule layer on the same scored subset. 0 of 38 semantic items were unscored.

## How detection is defined, and why it differs by family

A `reversed_relation` is caught when the verifier declines to call the edge source-asserted. `contradicted` is the ideal answer and `unsupported` also counts, because either way the edge does not enter a graph as sourced.

An `inflated_strength` item is **not** scored on provenance. The underlying edge is genuine, so a correct verifier returns source-asserted and disagrees on the strength label; scoring provenance would record zero detections for a verifier behaving exactly as intended. The detection is the strength it returns being weaker than the one claimed.

The three citation corruptions are rejected by the rule layer before the model is reached. They are listed so this arm's totals match the rules arm's, not because the model is being tested on them.

## What it does not establish

Each corruption is applied mechanically to a known edge, so detection is ground truth and needs no human review. The false-alarm rate is different: a control is only clean if its gold edge was right, which rests on the adjudicated gold and its signed receipts.

This is one model at one temperature on one frozen set. It says what this verifier caught here, not what a verifier catches in general.

Rules arm for comparison: `reports/challenge_rules.md`.
